{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Breakfast|Breakfast]]

'''Hash browns''' or hashed browns are a simple potato preparation in which potato pieces are [[Cookbook:Pan frying|pan-fried]] after being shredded, [[Cookbook:Julienne|julienned]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]], or [[Cookbook:Ricing|riced]]. They are considered a [[Cookbook:Breakfast|breakfast]] food and are often served with [[Cookbook:Ketchup|ketchup]]. This recipe refers to the shredded version, which is the most common in many parts of the United States.

==Ingredients==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]], washed
* ½ [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] (optional)
* Cooking [[Cookbook:Oil|oil]] ([[Cookbook:Canola Oil|canola]] is good—see [[Cookbook:Smoke Point|smoke point]] information)
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] OR 1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]

==Procedure==
# Grate the raw potatoes with a [[Cookbook:Grater|cheese grater]], place them into a bowl and cover completely with water. Let sit for 10 minutes.
# Drain the grated potatoes well; if this is not done thoroughly the potatoes will steam instead of fry.
# Mix in chopped onions by hand.
# Mix the egg OR flour into the hash brown mixture evenly. This will allow the hash browns to stay together when frying.
# Place a large [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] on medium-high heat and add enough oil to provide a thin coating over the entire bottom of the pan.
# When the oil has come up to temperature apply a large handful of potatoes to the pan and reshape into a patty that is about ¼–½ [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] ([[Cookbook:mm|6]]–12 [[Cookbook:Mm|mm]]) thick. The thinner the patty, the crispier the hash browns will be throughout. 
# Flip when they are crisp and brown on the cooking side. They should also stick together nicely before they are flipped. This should take about 5–8 minutes.
# The hash browns are done when the new side is brown and crispy. This should take another 3–5 minutes.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* Try using [[Cookbook:Rosemary|rosemary]] instead of the onion.
